questions.q: Why does Wrenhaven Retail assign different RTO and RPO targets to Tier 1 checkout versus Tier 3 reporting, instead of one target for the whole platform?
options: Because each tier's targets reflect its actual business impact -- checkout loses revenue instantly, reporting can wait a day
Because Azure requires different targets for databases versus dashboards
Because RTO and RPO can only be measured for database services
Because reporting workloads are technically incapable of being backed up
questions.explain: A tiered DR plan matches recovery targets to real business impact, so checkout gets tight numbers and reporting doesn't get over-built.

questions.q: What is the RTO and RPO assigned to Tier 1 (checkout) in this lab?
options: RTO 24 hours, RPO 24 hours
RTO 30 minutes, RPO 15 minutes
No RTO or RPO is assigned to Tier 1
RTO 5 minutes, RPO 1 minute
questions.explain: Checkout is handling money mid-transaction, so it gets the tightest targets of the three tiers: 5 minutes of downtime, 1 minute of data loss, at most.

questions.q: Why does failover-tier1.sh exist as a script rather than a written runbook for a human to follow?
options: Because Azure CLI commands cannot be documented in a runbook format
So the failover runs the same way every time instead of depending on a tired on-call engineer reading steps correctly at 3 a.m.
Because scripts are always faster than any manual command regardless of correctness
Because runbooks are forbidden by this course's DR policy
questions.explain: An automated failover removes the risk of a human executing a stressful, rarely-practiced procedure incorrectly under pressure.

questions.q: Why does the lab's first DR test fail over only a 5% canary slice of Tier 1 traffic, instead of the whole platform at once?
options: Because Front Door technically cannot route 100% of traffic to a secondary region
Because only 5% of Wrenhaven's customers use checkout
To scope the blast radius small enough to recover from if something is wrong, while still proving the real failover path works
Because Tier 2 and Tier 3 must always fail over before Tier 1 can be tested
questions.explain: A scoped test proves one tier's plan under a controlled, limited blast radius -- the responsible way to validate a failover before trusting it at full scale.

questions.q: What did the scoped Tier 1 test in this lab actually measure to decide pass or fail?
options: The real observed time-to-healthy and replica lag at promotion, compared against the 5-minute RTO and 1-minute RPO targets
Only whether the Azure CLI commands ran without throwing an error
Customer satisfaction survey scores collected after the test
Whether Tier 2 and Tier 3 were also failed over successfully
questions.explain: The test measured actual numbers -- 4m 12s to healthy and 38 seconds of replica lag -- against the targets, rather than assuming the plan worked.
